messages:
mike_r: noticing a p99 uplift in eu-prod around 03:00UTC, looks correlated with cross-region fallback to us-west. baseline p99 ~210ms -> spike to ~520ms for a 20m window.
anya: ugh, same window showed a KV cache miss rate jump on eu nodes? did we push any kernel changes?
rik: kernel selection logs show more fallbacks to the generic fp16 path when seq_len > 1024. fallback combined with cold KV miss could explain amplification.
sarah_l: timeline: 02:58 deploy-bot reported routing-policy tweak (canary). then 02:59 traffic rerouted to us-west for eu instances during a brief outage.
deploy-bot: canary: routing-policy v1.4.7 -> v1.4.8 deployed at 02:58:41 UTC, no errors during rollout.
jun: can we get a flame graph / profile for a representative request that hit p99? I want to see time breakdown: network / kernel / kv / batching wait.
mike_r: attached excerpt from profiler (trimmed):
```
[profile] request_id=tx-9834
total=523ms
  network: 42ms
  routing+queue: 87ms
  kv-fetch: 168ms (miss amplified via cross-region RTT)
  kernel-exec: 190ms (switched to generic kernel, no fast attention)
  post-proc: 36ms
```
anya: that kv-fetch is the killer — cross-region RTTs are 80-120ms roundtrip. with kv miss we add two roundtrips sometimes.
rik: microbatching makes this worse: if we increase microbatch size to hit throughput, queueing increases routing+queue which pushes seq_len distribution upward and triggers generic kernel selection.
sarah_l: so tradeoff: smaller microbatches -> lower queueing latency but worse throughput. larger -> higher throughput but p99 regression because of kernel/hotpath.
jun: quick experiment idea: temporarily bias routing to prefer regional capacity when latency-sensitive flag set. we can change routing policy weight for p95/p99 critical traffic.
mike_r: agree. also suggest adding a KV pre-warm on cross-region fallback: when routing switches, prefetch common prefixes for active routes. cheap heuristic: prefetch top-10 prefixes seen in last 5m.
anya: can we also add kernel hinting based on observed seq_len histogram? i.e., if >95th% seq_len > 512, prefer optimized kernel variant even if slightly higher memory to avoid fallback penalty.
rik: kernel hinting is doable but needs coordination with our kernel-selector. quick patch to prefer fast-attn for seq_len in (512,1024) reduced kernel-exec 190ms -> 120ms on bench.
sarah_l: runbook proposed: 1) rollback canary routing tweak or reduce weight to 0.7 at 03:30UTC 2) enable pre-warm for eu->us-west fallbacks 3) apply kernel hinting patch to canary runtime 4) run controlled throughput sweep to measure p95/p99 impact
jun: I'll own the sweep. target: microbatch sizes [1,4,8,16], measure p50/p95/p99, and record KV miss amplification with and without pre-warm.
mike_r: also collect per-kernel execution histograms and routing decision traces. add tags: seq_len_bin, kv_hit, fallback_region.
anya: small note on measurement: use steady-state traces for at least 10m per config to avoid noise. we saw spikes from autoscaler during previous runs.
rik: i've got a test build with kernel-hint flag: `--force-fast-attn-threshold=512` ready. will push to canary after we reduce routing weight.
sarah_l: priority: reduce customer-facing p99. if the canary rollback helps, we can iterate on hints + prewarm and then reintroduce routing tweak with safeguards.
mike_r: ok action items: rik -> push hint-canary; jun -> run sweep & report; anya -> implement pre-warm heuristic PR; sarah_l -> adjust routing weight and monitor; i'll draft a short incident-summary for CS.
deploy-bot: rollback: routing-policy v1.4.8 weight reduced to 0.7 at 03:31:12 UTC by sarah_l.
jun: started sweep at 03:35UTC, first batch (microbatch=1) baseline p99 ~220ms. will push results to the perf dashboard when done.
mike_r: thanks team. let's reconvene in #eng-runtime after the sweep (in ~45m). if anyone observes other hotspots drop a line here. :thumbsup:
